topic: Space-Filling Curves: The Bridge Between Dimensions

sections.title: The Dimensional Paradox (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Can a 1D line cover a 2D area?
Intuition suggests infinite folding is required.
We challenge the boundary between dimensions.
animations: Draw a 2D plane showing a unit square. (Color #FFFFFF)
Highlight the boundary line of the unit square. (Color #FF00FF)

sections.title: The Peano Curve Construction (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Divide the square into nine smaller squares.
Connect the centers in a specific path.
Iterate this process to refine the path.
animations: Create a grid and place a dot at center. (Color #FFFFFF)
Subdivide the square into 4 smaller quadrants. (Color #00FF00)
Connect the centers of the quadrants sequentially. (Color #FF00FF)

sections.title: The Hilbert Curve and Locality (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: The Hilbert curve improves on Peano.
animations: Draw a 2D plane with an 8x8 grid. (Color #FFFFFF)

sections.title: Real-World Applications (3:30-4:30)
lecture_lines: Database indexing benefits from this mapping.

sections.title: Summary and Philosophical Conclusion (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Curves bridge human perception and machines.
They are tools for computational efficiency.
